name: COMPARE
question: Are reusable intermittent catheters noninferior to single-use catheters for symptomatic UTI incidence in people with urinary retention?

design.blinding: Participants and research staff unblinded; outcome assessors masked
design.population: Patients aged 16 years or older with neurogenic or nonneurogenic urinary retention who had performed urethral clean intermittent catheterization at least twice daily for at least two weeks.
design.locator: Full text, Methods: Study Design, Participants, Intervention and Randomization; Table 1

verdictNote: Noninferiority met in the modified intention-to-treat analysis despite substantial reusable-arm discontinuation.
takeaway: In COMPARE's modified intention-to-treat analysis (191 single-use and 134 reusable participants of 386 randomized), sodium hypochlorite-disinfected reusable uncoated intermittent catheters were noninferior to single-use catheters for symptomatic UTI over one year (0.050 versus 0.054 per patient-month; difference −0.004, 95% CI −0.025 to 0.019).

reports.label: One-year primary report
reports.citation: van Veen FEE, Christiaans CHH, Berendsen SA, et al. Single-Use vs Reusable Catheters for Intermittent Catheterization in Patients With Urinary Retention: The COMPARE Randomized Clinical Trial. *JAMA Netw Open.* 2026;9(6):e2620871. doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.20871
reports.followUp: One year; modified intention-to-treat mean 11.4 months reusable and 12.0 months single-use

results.measure: UTIs per patient-month in modified intention-to-treat analysis; absolute incidence-rate difference (reusable minus single-use); noninferiority margin +0.07 UTIs per patient-month
results.note: Noninferiority required the upper bound of the two-sided 95% CI to be below +0.07.
results.locator: Full text, Methods: Statistical Analysis; Results: Primary Outcome; Table 2

results.measure: Patients with at least one UTI during modified intention-to-treat follow-up
results.note: The source calls the modified intention-to-treat population n=326, although these arm denominators sum to 325.

results.endpoint: Symptomatic UTI incidence, intention-to-treat sensitivity analysis
results.measure: UTIs per patient-month; absolute incidence-rate difference (reusable minus single-use)
results.note: Prespecified sensitivity analysis of patients who initiated assigned treatment; upper confidence bound remains below the +0.07 margin.
results.locator: Full text, Methods: Statistical Analysis; Results: Primary Outcome; Table 2

results.endpoint: Symptomatic UTI incidence, per-protocol sensitivity analysis
results.measure: UTIs per patient-month; absolute incidence-rate difference (reusable minus single-use)
results.note: Prespecified sensitivity analysis of one-year completers without major deviations; upper confidence bound remains below the +0.07 margin.
results.locator: Full text, Methods: Statistical Analysis; Results: Primary Outcome; Table 2

results.endpoint: Complier-average causal effect estimate of UTI incidence
results.measure: Estimated absolute difference in UTIs per patient-month accounting for reusable-catheter nonadherence
results.note: The confidence interval includes the +0.07 noninferiority margin.
results.locator: Full text, Results: Primary Outcome; eTable 2 described in text

results.measure: Intermittent Self-Catheterization Questionnaire score at week 52; mean difference (reusable minus single-use)
results.note: Arm-specific scores were not given in the article text.

delivery.label: Reusable catheter protocol
delivery.value: Uncoated Cliny catheters for males and PureCath catheters for females; rinse with tap water before and after use, store in 2% sodium hypochlorite solution renewed daily, replace every two weeks, and permit single-use catheters for at most 20% of weekly catheterizations.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods: Intervention and Randomization

delivery.label: Lead-in and analysis population
delivery.value: Six-week lead-in; 326/386 entered the reported modified intention-to-treat population (191 single-use and 134 reusable reported in the primary outcome table, summing to 325).
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods: Study Design and Statistical Analysis; Results: Study Population; Table 2

delivery.label: Reusable-arm discontinuation
delivery.value: 72/185 (39%) discontinued; 39/185 (21.1%) reported ease-of-use challenges and 13/185 (7.0%) urethral irritation as discontinuation reasons.
delivery.locator: Full text, Results: Study Population; Figure 1

delivery.label: Reusable catheter adherence and continuation
delivery.value: Mean reusable use was 88.6% of catheterizations in the intention-to-treat population; 113/193 randomized reusable-arm patients completed one year, and 105/113 (92.9%) completers preferred to continue reuse.
delivery.locator: Full text, Results: Study Population and Adherence to Protocol; Figure 1
